finding.claim: The --json output is a dict built by hand in the command body, with behind derived there. .claude/rules/pydantic-boundaries.md says an output shape a caller depends on is built as a typed object, not assembled as a dict, and every other result verb here prints json.dumps(asdict(dataclass)). Give Nudge a behind field (or a small frozen dataclass for the JSON shape) and print json.dumps(asdict(found)), so a renamed key breaks at the type gate and the shape lives in summary.py with its docstring.

fixes.change: Nudge carries behind (derived from concepts) and calls its text nudge, so --json prints the dataclass as is
--json prints json.dumps(asdict(found)) instead of a dict built in the command body; the keys are unchanged
